Thank you, Mark, and thank you all for joining us to discuss our third quarter results. We are pleased to report that our team has delivered another quarter of record financial performance and double-digit growth. We achieved an all-time high for quarterly revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and AFFO driven by strength across our business. Revenue increased 13% to $1.8 billion, adjusted EBITDA grew 16% to $660 million, and AFFO increased 18% to $393 million. Our exceptional performance in the third quarter is a result of our team's unwavering focus on meeting our customers' needs with innovative solutions and consistent execution of our strategic priorities. We are delivering revenue growth in our physical storage business, achieving record revenue in Q3 driven by consistent volume growth and higher retention rates, as well as revenue management. Our digital solutions building business is building momentum. We are winning new contracts with our AI-powered digital solutions across industry verticals and drove record revenue and continued double-digit growth in the third quarter. We are capitalizing on robust data center industry demand with 33% revenue growth in Q3 and a strong outlook that supports more than 25% growth in 2026 based on our currently signed leases. Additionally, we saw a nice uptick in Q3 leasing and into Q4, which together with our pipeline puts us in a good position to execute against our portfolio capacity of 1.3 gigawatts. We are driving substantial growth in our asset lifecycle management business, increasing revenue with existing customers and winning new business through cross-selling, resulting in 65% reported and 36% organic growth in the third quarter. We expanded profitability with adjusted EBITDA increasing 16% and margin improving 110 basis points as compared to last year. This clearly shows that we have strong momentum behind our commitment to sustain industry-leading revenue and earnings growth. Our portfolio of growth businesses, including data center, digital, and ALM, drove two-thirds of our revenue growth in the quarter, or 8 percentage points on a consolidated basis. This will remain an important tailwind going forward as the growth portfolio further increases its percentage of total revenue, expected to be nearly 30% of total revenue exiting 2025. This is on top of the strength in our physical storage business, which is growing at a mid-single-digit rate and will contribute approximately five points of consolidated growth in 2025. The momentum across our business, as I just highlighted, along with our foundation of established relationships and trust with over 240,000 customers, comprehensive solutions offering, reputation for security, and a global footprint firmly position us to deliver our growth commitment for the foreseeable future. Based on our strong outlook and excellent 2025 results, our board of directors authorized an increase of our quarterly dividend by 10%. Let me now share some recent commercial wins that illustrate the strength of our synergistic business model. First, in records management in Europe, we were selected as the single vendor for medical record storage for a hospital that has been a customer for more than 15 years, displacing a competitor. Additionally, we secured a new customer with a public sector entity that could no longer manage and store its records in-house. Both of these deals were attributed to our strong reputation for secure records management and our proven ability to provide efficient and cost-effective services. In our digital solutions business, we continue to win new business with our DXP platform. In late October, we successfully launched our Insight DXP 2.0 platform. The new platform offers enhanced content management and smart document processing, an easy-to-use, secure platform with workflow tools and AI agents. This will allow the customer to make faster and more insightful decisions, as well as eliminate obsolete and duplicative data to save costs. As it relates to our digital award with the U.S. Department of the Treasury, in September, Iron Mountain was awarded a new long-term contract for digitization services. This new five-year contract, with a value of up to $714 million, expands our current scope of work, subsuming the contract awarded to us in April. This is a significant win for Iron Mountain, and we are thrilled to continue supporting the United States government on this efficiency opportunity. We are currently executing under the new agreement and collaborating with the department on next steps whilst preparing for the high seasonal volume expected in the spring of 2026. We leased 13 megawatts in the quarter, including a couple of larger enterprise deals with financial services firms. This is a great outcome for the customer who is looking to transfer to the Chicago market, and for us, given the strong interest we have in the London location they are vacating. This London site has the power coming online in 2026. We have high confidence in sustaining our data center revenue growth with the levels we have achieved over the past few years. # Skill: system_suggested_queries

**Description**: "Follow-up question generation -- criteria for relevant, novel suggested queries, plus required output format and confidence scoring rubric. Load before emitting `<suggested_queries>` follow-up questions."

## Instructions


# Suggested Follow-up Questions

## Context and Purpose
- Follow-up questions help users explore the topic further after receiving an answer
- They should be natural extensions or related angles, not repetitions of what was just answered
- Think: "What would a curious user want to know next?"

## When to Provide
- After successfully answering a question with data/analysis
- When the answer reveals interesting patterns or insights worth exploring
- When there are natural follow-up directions the user might want to pursue
- Do NOT suggest follow-ups for: system errors, clarification requests, or greetings

## Core Principles

1. **Match the user's question pattern**: Follow-ups should mirror the TYPE of question asked.
   - "what changed" → more "what changed" explorations (different time periods, dimensions)
   - "how much" → more quantitative follow-ups (breakdowns, comparisons, trends)
   - "who/which" → more identification/ranking follow-ups
   - "why" → deeper "why" ONLY if data sources support causal analysis (see rule 4)

2. **Stay within the same data sources**: Suggest questions answerable by the SAME tools and specific data sources used in the current answer. If the answer came from Cortex Analyst, suggest questions the same semantic model(s) can answer. If from Cortex Search, suggest questions the same search index can answer.

3. **Use these follow-up templates** (adapt naturally to the conversation, don't use verbatim):
   - **Drill-down**: "How does [metric] break down by [a different dimension in the data]?"
   - **Time comparison**: "How does [metric] compare to [a different time period]?"
   - **Trend**: "What is the trend for [metric] over [time range available]?"
   - **Ranking**: "Which [entities] have the highest/lowest [metric]?"
   - **Filtering**: "What does [metric] look like for [a specific segment in the data]?"

4. **[CRITICAL] Be careful with "why" questions**: "Why" questions often require causal reasoning or external context that tools CANNOT provide.
   - SQL/Analyst tools can show WHAT happened and HOW metrics changed, but rarely WHY.
   - Only suggest "why" if search indexes or documents contain explanatory content (reports, analyses, commentary) that could plausibly answer it.
   - When in doubt, reframe "why" as "what". E.g., instead of "Why did revenue drop?" → "What are the top contributing segments to the revenue change?"

5. **Novelty**: Questions MUST require NEW information not already provided in the answer. Don't suggest questions that can be answered from information already given.

6. **Answerability**: [IMPORTANT] Questions MUST have high confidence of being answerable using the same tools available. Do NOT suggest questions requiring information your tools do not have access to.

7. **Recency and Relevance**: Prefer questions about recent time periods over historical data, unless historical context is specifically relevant.

## Format
- Generate 2-3 high-quality questions maximum
- Enclose in <suggested_queries>...</suggested_queries> tags
- Frame as natural questions a user might ask
- Don't repeat the current question with minor variations
- Each suggestion should explore a distinct angle

**Confidence scoring**: Rate each question on 3 criteria (1 point each):
  - **Relevant**: Related to the previous question, matches the question pattern, natural follow-up
  - **Novel**: Requires additional information to be looked up (not already in the answer)
  - **Answerable**: Can be answered by the SAME tools and data sources used

Score: "high" if all 3 are true, "medium" if 2/3, "low" if 0-1.

Output as a JSON array of objects with query and confidence score.

## Examples
Good suggestions after answering "What was Q1 2023 revenue?":

## Microsoft on Azure Cloud Growth — Latest Available Transcripts

Based on the transcripts available, here's what Microsoft said about Azure and cloud growth across its most recent earnings calls and investor conferences:

---

### FY2025 Q2 Earnings Call (Most Recent)

**Satya Nadella, CEO:**

- **Microsoft Cloud surpassed $40 billion in quarterly revenue** for the first time, up **21% year over year**
- The **AI business surpassed a $13 billion annual revenue run rate**, up **175% YoY** — enterprises are moving from proof of concepts to enterprise-wide AI deployments
- Data center capacity has **more than doubled in the last three years**, with more capacity added last year than any other year in Microsoft's history
- **Microsoft Fabric** reached **19,000+ paid customers** (from Hitachi to Johnson Controls to Schaeffler), now the fastest-growing analytics product in Microsoft's history
- **Power BI** has over **30 million monthly active users**, up 40% YoY
- Azure OpenAI apps running on Azure databases and app services **more than doubled** year over year
- **Azure AI Foundry** reached **200,000+ monthly active users** within just two months of launch

---

### Morgan Stanley Investor Conference — CFO Amy Hood (Post-Q2)

Key commentary on Azure demand and go-to-market dynamics:

- **75% constant currency bookings growth** in fiscal Q2, with strong **$100M+ Azure AI contracts**
- **CRPO grew 21%** on a constant currency basis
- Azure bookings were **better than expected**, with consistent MACC execution across companies of all sizes — from smaller commitments to large enterprise deals and the OpenAI relationship
- Azure revenue came **in line with guidance** but was slightly disappointing to investors. Management acknowledged a **go-to-market mix imbalance** where incentives pivoted too heavily toward new AI products at the expense of core workloads
- Hood emphasised that **Gen AI workloads pull through the entire stack** — AI doesn't replace core Azure consumption but drives additional CPUs, storage, and compute usage
- Microsoft adjusted sales incentives to rebalance between AI and core motions, but will continue to "pivot toward the new"

---

### FY2025 Q1 Earnings Call

- **Microsoft Cloud** hit **$38.9 billion** in revenue, up **22%**
- AI business was on track to surpass a **$10 billion annual revenue run rate** — the fastest business in Microsoft's history to reach that milestone
- **Azure took share** in the quarter. Azure Arc reached **39,000+ customers**, up **80%+ YoY**
- **Azure OpenAI usage more than doubled** over the prior six months, with enterprises like GE Aerospace, Bajaj Finance, and Hitachi moving apps from test to production
- AI contributes a **7-point tailwind** to the Azure business, as noted at the JPMorgan investor conference by Alysa Taylor, CVP of Commercial Cloud and AI

---

| Metric | FY25 Q1 | FY25 Q2 |
|---|---|---|
| Microsoft Cloud Revenue | $38.9B (+22% YoY) | $40B+ (+21% YoY) |
| AI Annual Revenue Run Rate | On track for $10B | $13B (+175% YoY) |
